description: A high-performance, lightweight Entity Component System (ECS) for C#. Archetype and chunk based storage, source-generated ForEach queries, inline component buffers, tags, change filters, multithreaded query execution, SIMD-friendly handles and command buffers — with zero external dependencies on .NET 8.
releaseNotes: 3.10.0: the entity map moved to native memory: 16 bytes per id with no object references (was 28), so creating entities allocates almost nothing on the GC heap and growing the database triggers no collections; loading a world without Reserve is about 1.5x faster, Create with Reserve about 1.6x, Destroy plus recycling about 1.3x. Freed ids are recycled oldest first as before, without the queue that allocated as it grew. Reserving past MaxEntities now always throws (it depended on spare room in a pooled array), and creating entities after Dispose throws ObjectDisposedException. 3.9.0: writing a [TrackChanges] component no longer bumps the global change version when its chunk is already marked newer than anything a change filter has seen (change filters report the same chunks; tracked Set is about 1.7x faster, creating entities with a tracked component about 1.5x faster, and a CommandBuffer Commit marks each chunk once); Read, Write, Set, TryRead, ReadBuffer and WriteBuffer by entity do one dependent load less; CommandBuffer Commit skips the create and change passes when there are none. ChangeFilter.GlobalChangeVersions holds a second row (entries 256-511) with the newest version any filter has consumed. 3.8.0: structural changes are 1.6-3.3x faster - every Create overload, Clone, Add/Remove moves, Destroy, and CommandBuffer recording and Commit (CommandBuffer creates are about 3x faster and allocate about 60% less); Clone copies the source entity even when allocating the clone's id grows the entity map; Move(entity, signature) defaults the components it adds instead of keeping a previous occupant's values; a CommandBuffer reused after Clear, or after Set and Destroy on the same entity, keeps every entity's buffered values apart; CommandBuffer.Create with three or more buffer components keeps every buffer; EntityDatabase.Dispose and TrimExcess free archetype chunk memory; buffered dynamic buffers that are cancelled or never applied release their heap memory. 3.7.2: Clear forgets ids recycled by earlier destroys - entities created after a Clear start again from id 0 and are found by id. 3.7.1: an entity that loses a managed component keeps the remaining managed components paired with their own data - Remove/AddAndRemove no longer throw ArrayTypeMismatchException or copy a neighbouring component's value. 3.7.0: ParallelJobRunner signals only the workers a call needs (a one-job call never leaves the calling thread), runs jobs a worker hasn't started on the caller, and parks idle workers instead of spinning - more threads than cores no longer costs milliseconds per parallel call; parallel queries claim chunks from one shared list (a preempted thread no longer stalls the join) and are allocation-free in steady state; UntrackedWriteHandle and Chunk.MarkChanged<T>() to write tracked components without marking every chunk; generated ForEach/ForEachChunk honour change filters; a destroy carries the moved entity's pending changes; chunks past 32 KB keep their columns apart (int offsets); fresh entity ids start at version 0; a stale EntityData throws instead of reaching another archetype (chunk arrays are no longer pooled); EntityDatabase() and EntityDatabaseOptions.Default; TrimExcess on an empty database. 3.6.0: parallel queries execute one fork/join across all matching archetypes (was one per archetype); Archetype.Reserve zero-initializes unmanaged chunk memory.
title: EntitiesDb
